The identity morphism of an object $g \in \Ob(G)$ is defined by
$$i(g) = (1,g). $$
Finally, the composite of the morphisms 
$$\alpha = (h,g) \maps g \to t(h)g \qquad \text{and}\qquad
\beta = (h',t(h)g) \maps t(h)g \to t(h'h)g'$$ 
is defined to be
$$ \beta \circ \alpha =  (h'h, g) \maps g \to t(h'h) g $$
It is easy to check that with these definitions, $\G$ is a $2$-group.
